reading.body:
This entry is not a data center and should not be counted as one. The name describes a web development business, its domain now redirects to a parked for-sale page, and the coordinates resolve to a different current occupant, Hole Hunter Industries, on East Gray Road in Scottsdale.

The pattern is a mistagged point rather than a facility. A small web design firm was recorded in OpenStreetMap as data center infrastructure, and the tag outlived the business. The stored address sits several miles from the other eight rows in its batch, so no shared building connects them.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a counting problem, not a capacity one. Any tally of Arizona data centers that includes this row overstates the building stock, and building stock is the layer that power and compute ultimately depend on. A single false positive is small, but the error mode is systematic: tags persist after the underlying business disappears.

What the data does not show is how many other entries carry the same defect. It gives one confirmed case, with a parked domain, a mismatched reverse geocode, and no published specifications, and nothing about the scale of the problem beyond it.
